Nobody likes being preached to.

That's probably what it feels like to them; as if you're beginning the conversation with "you're wrong and I want you to understand why."

Nobody likes that. Nobody thinks they're wrong, and someone flat out saying they're wrong is basically saying you think they're stupid for not figuring it out.

You're basically "trying to convert them" in their eyes, even though you'd say it's not converting.

And that's just not what friends are *for.*

There are many, many, many things in this world that it's not worth arguing over, because you'll never change their mind with just a conversation anyway. Something THAT big, like a religion, or economic doctrine, or political stance...those are often dictated by someone's absolute core values and experiences. Nothing short of that will change their mind, certainly not some prat nagging them with what feels like empty words and condescension.

My best friend as a child came from a VERY religious household, I didn't (parents were religious but not "church every Sunday" devout, and I pretty quickly realized I didn't *really* believe in it) but it never came up. He was just my friend, the friend I play Super Smash Brothers with and played on the swing set and tag and all that; who cared what he *believed?* He wasn't my friend because of that.

If you keep this up your friends will simply not want to be around you. Decide if you *absolutely* need everyone close to you to think *exactly* as you do, or learn to love who people are and not always the conclusions they draw about the world...especially if those conclusions aren't actually harming anyone around them.

Sometimes a digital platform, to make things "look better" or easier to follow, misrepresents things.

All damage is done simultaneously. So the life gained from Lifelink happens at the exact same moment that the damage is being done, so the opponent never went to 0 life in the first place.

Alternatively, nothing ever dies in the middle of a card resolving either. Like, say you have a 4/4 Army token, and you cast a specific spell and target it. Does it die because you did 4 damage to it? No, because the game will not check if it dies until after the spell completely resolves, so at the end you're left with an 8/8 Army which has 4 damage done to it, and it lives.

So you could even think of it as the game (not just the digital platform, but actual rules) doesn't check if the opponent dies until after the Lifelink life gain happens.

Another example of misrepresentation is how it marks damage on creatures, it makes it appear as if they are losing Toughness when they take damage but that's not how it works. A 4/4 that has taken 2 damage is not a 4/2 until end of turn, it's a 4/4 with 2 damage marked on it. And a card like [[High Alert]] makes it look like 0 Power Defenders have Power equal to their Toughness during the combat phase but they actually still have only 0 Power, it's just that you no longer calculate their damage based on their Power anymore.

Let’s put it this way: say you and the opponent have been going at it for a while and both have a bunch of lands and have traded resources quite a bit. Neither of you has cards in hand, but you have two creatures out and he has an empty board so you have the advantage. For simplicity let’s say you’re mono Green and the opponent is mono Black. 

He top decks a powerful planeswalker and uses her -4 to wipe your board. Now what do you do?

Without a card like a specific high-impact creature, situations that can happen are: 

* You draw a card that can hit Planeswalkers like a direct damage spell but you can’t use it until you draw a creature. The planeswalker ticks up and makes a blocker. 
* You draw and play a non-Haste creature. The planeswalker ticks up and makes a blocker. Next turn do you even swing, and what at if you do? Either way big loss for you. 
* Maybe you get a Trampler that threatens the planeswalker when it can attack next turn. But if they draw removal...you still have no board. The planeswalker ticks up and makes a blocker.
* Even if you get a Trampler and attack next turn and they draw badly, they’ve still taken out two of your creatures, drawn a card, and made you attack a target that’s not their life that turn, all in one card. Huge tempo loss for you and you have fewer cards than them now. 

You’d need perfect draws to recover from that. Or play a specific high-impact creature and get back in the fight. 

Maybe that specific creature doesn’t need *all* of its abilities but it is the only answer Green has that works, so it at the very least needs Haste, unblockable by weenies, and hits PWs when it hits face.

You realize that plenty of colors have direct answers to PWs that cost less than 4 mana right? Murderous Rider. Angrath’s Rampage. Prison Realm. Conclave Tribunal. Almost any counter spell. Bedevil. Spark Harvest. Brazen Borrower. Etc. Green having answer at 4 on a creature is not that weird. 

Aside from QB then Green doesn’t have a single answer *at all* because it requires two cards. A spell, and a creature powerful enough for it to matter. Hell, Green doesn’t even really have a competitive Trampler at the moment either. That really, really leaves Green unable to compete with a control deck with PWs because they need a threat to stick to actually use a removal card. 

My last point isn’t that they just got value, but that without QB, the Green player would need a lot of luck to have not lost the game already. If Liliana dies, they got value. If she doesn’t, the Black player just wins from free 2/2s every turn and card draw. 

Most Planeswalkers get value immediately but if they can stay perpetually you’re hosed. And Green has no reliable way to prevent that aside from QB. Try playing a Green deck without QB in Historic against Esper Control and see how it goes for you.
